messages:
Samir: noticing p99 wobble in usw1 starting 02:10 UTC. not a single noisy tenant this time  looks like many small warmups aligned and caused kvcache regen + NIC tx spikes across racks. any quick thoughts?

Nia: saw it on heatmaps. cross-host kvcache correlation is high. When lots of tenants pre-warm simultaneously we end up with regen storms that look like one big attacker.

Toby: short term we can: (A) apply very short (30-90m) soft-quarantine + egress limit to top n offenders, (B) enable router-side smoothing (per-tenant rate weights) to spread requests over time, (C) offer a staggered burst-credit flow for heavy warmups. I like (A)+(B) immediately.

Samir: agree. let's avoid carving right away since rebalancing could make the noise worse. Nia, can you pick top-8 correlated tenants and apply 60m soft-quarantine with local preemptible fallback? Use moderate caps so jobs still progress.

Nia: running quick patch now:
````
rwdctl tenant update tenant-{id} --egress-limit 90mbps --soft-quarantine true --quarantine-ttl 60m --fallback preemptible
````
I'll iterate through the top-8 and post telemetry.

OpsBot: Created ticket INF-6789: "aligned warmups -> short soft-quarantine + router smoothing". Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/aligned-warmup-mitigation

Toby: For router smoothing, I'll flip on a temporary per-tenant token bucket so the control plane spreads warmup requests across a 5m window rather than letting everyone hit at once. That should cut the instantaneous egress peaks.

Product-Emma: on product side, customers keep asking for predictable warmup windows. We should design a "staggered burst" offering where tenants can reserve a time window and either pay or burn a credit. Ideally it offers: pre-warm handshake, guaranteed small kvcache pin, and a soft egress carve if needed.

Samir: good idea. For infra follow-up: (1) RFC for burst-credit model with APIs for scheduling and pre-warm handshake, (2) router-weighting heuristics to smooth spontaneous warmups, (3) dashboard for burst-ticket usage and cross-host kvcache correlation. Toby/Nia pick up halves?

Toby: I'll prototype router-weighting + token-bucket smoothing and add a quick flag to enable per-tenant smoothing windows. Will include rollback if p99 doesn't improve.

Nia: I'll own the dashboard + detector that flags >3-host kvcache correlation within a 2m window, and I'll collect telemetry from the quarantine patches.

Product-Emma: I'll draft the customer UX and pricing options: pay-per-window, subscription credits, or free limited quota. Also sketch out an SLA for pre-warm guarantees vs best-effort.

Samir: Short term ops: keep the soft-quarantine + smoothing for 60m. If p99 doesn't drop by >10% within 10m, escalate to a tiny 1-2 GPU carve with strict egress. Nia, post numbers in 10.

Nia: Initial after patches: p99 down ~14%, host nic tx drops reduced ~38%, kvcache_eviction rate down ~30%. Token-bucket smoothing shows flattening on router heatmap. Leaving policies on for 60m.

Toby: Nice. I'll open RFC stub for router-weighting and smoothing and include simple config examples (+ test plan).

OpsBot: INF-6789 updated: assignees Toby (router prototype), Nia (monitoring + dashboard), Product-Emma (burst offering UX/pricing).
